title: First conversation
summary: Tell me about your land, house or idea. I will tell you honestly whether I can help, and what the next step would be.
responsibilities:
A 30-minute call or site coffee
Your questions, answered plainly
What working together would look like
A written follow-up, even if we do not proceed
requirements:
The address or a few photos
Your rough timeline
What you hope the project makes possible
body:
Tell me about your land, house or idea. I will tell you honestly whether I can help, and what the next step would be.

I am one architect and I take four to six full projects a year. These shorter engagements are how most projects start — and sometimes they are all you need.

This is a fictional example. Marlowe Architecture is not a real practice.

title: Feasibility study
salary: Fixed fee, quoted after our call
summary: Can this lot take an ADU? Should this house be remodeled or rebuilt? A short study with sketches and rough costs.
responsibilities:
Site or house visit
Zoning, tree and permit notes
Sketch options in plan
Rough cost ranges from a builder
requirements:
A survey, if you have one
Old plans or listing photos
Your must-haves and deal-breakers

title: Design consultation
salary: Fixed fee, half or full day
summary: A working session on a plan you already have: light, flow, materials, and the decisions that are expensive to undo.
responsibilities:
Review of your plans, in person
Marked-up sketches during the session
A written list of recommendations
Material and porch/shade advice
requirements:
Your current drawings
Photos of the house and yard
The decisions keeping you up at night
